content.overview: Section 2 is the definition gateway for the Companies Act, 2013. A defined term controls later sections unless the context otherwise requires.
content.glance: Section 2 is the definition gateway for the Companies Act, 2013. A defined term controls later sections unless the context otherwise requires.
content.study: Section 2 defines the persons, securities, offices and relationships used throughout the Act. Exam and practice analysis should identify the exact clause rather than a textbook label. Particularly load-bearing clauses include company (s. 2(20)), one person company (s. 2(62)), private company (s. 2(68)), public company (s. 2(71)), holding company (s. 2(46)), subsidiary (s. 2(87), including the control and majority-share tests), small company (s. 2(85)), related party (s. 2(76)), key managerial personnel (s. 2(51)), officer who is in default (s. 2(60)), net worth (s. 2(57)) and deposit (s. 2(31)). Several thresholds, especially small company and related party, have been amended by later Amendment Acts and rules; the numeric threshold in force on the relevant date must be checked before advice. A body incorporated outside India is not a company under s. 2(20) merely because it carries on business in India; foreign-company provisions in Chapter XXII are separate.

examples.title: Private company test
examples.body: A company which by its articles restricts transfer, limits members (other than OPC) to 200, and prohibits public invitation for securities, is a private company under s. 2(68), subject to the statutory exceptions.

examples.title: Subsidiary control
examples.body: Holding more than one-half of the total voting power, or control of board composition, can make the other company a subsidiary under s. 2(87).

distinctions: Company under s. 2(20) is a statutory registration concept. It is not the same as a partnership firm, LLP, or foreign company.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Which clause decides whether a company is private?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 2(68), read with the articles and the statutory carve-outs. Do not use the old Companies Act, 1956 member limit.

caseLaw.name: Salomon v A Salomon & Co Ltd
caseLaw.point: Section 2 defines company by reference to incorporation. Salomon is the authority that incorporation creates a person distinct from the members.
